sub_chapter_briefs.title: 2 A.M. and the Dead Bands
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara sits at her receiver in the pre-dawn dark, running her nightly scan of the shortwave bands — all silence, as always — when the needle on 7.850 MHz twitches and holds. She does not move. She listens.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: Mara sits at her receiver in the pre-dawn dark, running her nightly scan of the shortwave bands — all silence, as always — when the needle on 7.850 MHz twitches and holds. She does not move. She listens.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 2 — Call to Adventure (first contact: the signal arrives unbidden into the silence Mara has accepted as permanent)
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Mara's fortified farmhouse — the receiver room, a former kitchen stripped to its studs and rebuilt around salvaged equipment; 2 a.m., no light except the amber glow of the dial
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Hyperalert stillness — the specific quality of attention Mara reserves for things that should not exist
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: The Call to Adventure lands: the signal on 7.850 MHz is the disruption that will end Mara's static existence and begin the journey west; it is undeniable because it is technically impossible, and Mara knows exactly why it is impossible

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Signal Architecture
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara works through the night with pencil and logbook, stripping the signal down to its components — carrier wave, modulation pattern, repeat interval, bearing estimate. She rules out every natural and artifact explanation one by one. Her final notation, underlined twice: intentional. powered. west. 300–400 miles.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 2 — Call to Adventure (the call is confirmed and quantified: this is not noise, it is a summons)
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: Same receiver room; the hour advances toward 4 a.m.; the logbook fills with Mara's private shorthand; a mechanical watch ticks on the shelf above the receiver
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Focused dread — the excitement of a technician who has found something extraordinary and the fear of someone who understands exactly what finding it means
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Establishes Mara's core competence and the signal's reality before the story can complicate either; the technical confirmation is the threshold moment that makes refusal a choice rather than a default

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Fire She Does Not Light
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara tears the logbook pages out, holds them over the cold stove, and does not strike the match. She stands there long enough that her hand stops shaking. Then she folds the pages and puts them in her coat pocket. She tells herself this is not a decision.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 3 — Refusal of the Call (the refusal is enacted physically — she almost destroys the evidence — and psychologically — she refuses to name what keeping it means)
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The kitchen stove, cold; the farmhouse around her is dark and silent; first grey light beginning at the window
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Paralysis at the edge of commitment — the specific terror of someone who knows that knowing something changes everything
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: The refusal is rooted in Mara's wound: she left Dani to chase equipment and he died; going west means leaving again, and she does not yet know how to hold that; the unlit match is the novel's first image of a choice deferred

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Memory Is Its Own Transmission
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: By full daylight, Mara has rewritten every page from memory into a fresh logbook — neater than the originals, more complete, with a bearing calculation she did not have the first time. She stares at what she has done. The signal repeats on the receiver behind her, right on schedule.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 3 — Refusal of the Call collapses into Stage 2 — the refusal fails; the call is louder than the fear
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The receiver room again, morning light; the fresh logbook open on the workbench; the receiver still running
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Rueful self-knowledge — Mara recognizes that she has already decided, that the rewriting was not compulsion but choice, and that she is afraid of herself for it
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: The escalating lie thread begins here in embryo: Mara has destroyed and recreated evidence, a habit of self-deception about her own motives that will compound when she makes the promise to Tomás in Chapter 2 and begins qualifying it immediately; ESCALATION SEED — starts: Mara tells herself she is 'just documenting,' not deciding (Ch. 1); must reappear: Mara makes a promise to Tomás she privately hedges (Ch. 2); explodes: the hedged promise costs someone something irreversible (Ch. 6)

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Knock
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: A knock at the farmhouse door — Tomás Reyes, two days early on his courier route, sheltering from weather. Mara lets him in. He sees the receiver running, hears the signal cycling through its repeat, and goes very still in a way that mirrors her own stillness. He says: 'That's not atmospheric.' He does not say what it is. He looks at her and waits.

sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 2 — Call to Adventure widens: a second witness arrives who recognizes the signal's significance, transforming Mara's private discovery into a shared crisis and making the journey suddenly possible
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The farmhouse door and receiver room; mid-morning; rain beginning outside
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: The specific unease of a secret becoming shared — relief and exposure at once; the scene ends on suspension, not resolution
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Sets up Chapter 2 directly: Tomás has recognized something Mara has not yet named aloud; his military signals background will identify the encryption pattern as the hook that opens the next chapter; the dramatic question propelling the reader forward is not whether the signal is real — that is confirmed — but what Tomás knows about it that Mara does not
